newsitem.title: UK: Row delays Chinese listing on London exchange - FT.
newsitem.headline: Row delays Chinese listing on London exchange - FT.

text.p: An argument over pricing has delayed the listing of the first-ever Chinese company to be traded on London's stock exchange, the Financial Times newspaper reported on Monday.
It said Beijing Datang Power Generation was scheduled to float simultaneously in London and Hong Kong later this month on an issue of 1.2 billion shares worth $300 million.

But the lead managers, which included Salomon Brothers and British merchant bank Kleinwort Benson, were unable to reach an agreement on a suitable price after a "difficult" meeting in Beijing on Thursday.

The newspaper, quoting unnamed bankers involved in the deal, said Salomon had confirmed the float had been postponed. But it gave the "official" reason as the current weakness of trading in Chinese shares on the Hong Kong market.
